data.name: Header_LockTooltip
data.value: Lock: hide account details and stop automation until you unlock

data.name: Appearance_LanguageDescription
data.value: English is the only language included in this preview. Follow Windows uses your Windows display language once a translation for it is included, and mirrors the window for a right-to-left language. The two pseudo-locale choices are for testing: text from the catalog is shown marked, and anything shown plain is not translated yet. A language change applies at once and is saved, like a theme.

data.name: Appearance_CloseButtonExitsDescription
data.value: Off by default: the close button keeps the manager running in the tray, and one click on the tray icon reopens it. When on, the close button stops this manager the same way as Exit. Save settings to apply.

data.name: Appearance_LockWhenIdleDescription
data.value: Off by default. When on, the manager locks like Lock after that long without keyboard or mouse input in its windows, including while it is in the tray: account details are hidden and automation and the launch queue stop until you unlock. A sign-in or native trial in progress counts as activity. Save settings to apply.

data.name: Appearance_PublicNetworkGuard
data.value: Hold launches on a public network

data.name: Appearance_PublicNetworkGuardDescription
data.value: Off by default. When on, Zenith watches which network profile Windows gives the active connection. While a connected network with internet access is filed Public (café, hotel or airport Wi-Fi, for example), new launches are held with that reason and the dashboard locks like Lock, with a notice. Held requests start again on their own once the network is Private or Domain; the dashboard stays locked until you unlock it. Windows tells Zenith when the network changes, so nothing polls, and no network name is read or kept. Save settings to apply.

data.name: Appearance_DiscordAlertsDescription
data.value: Off by default. When on, Zenith posts a short message to one Discord webhook you save below when a client crashes, stops responding or is disconnected, and when a launch batch has finished. Messages carry only the account's label, the place and counts: never log lines, links or anything from Roblox. Alerts that happen within two seconds share one message, at most 50 wait to be sent, and a failed send is reported once and not retried. Panic stops the alerts until you choose Resume alerts; Lock leaves them running. Save settings to apply.

data.name: Appearance_WebhookUrlTooltip
data.value: Paste the webhook URL Discord shows for the channel. It is kept protected on this PC and never shown again.

data.name: Appearance_SaveWebhookTooltip
data.value: Check the pasted URL and keep it protected

data.name: Appearance_SendTestAlertTooltip
data.value: Post a test message to the saved webhook

data.name: Appearance_ResumeAlertsTooltip
data.value: Send alerts again after Panic or a refused webhook

data.name: Appearance_DiscordPresence
data.value: Show Zenith in your Discord status

data.name: Appearance_DiscordPresenceDescription
data.value: Off by default. When on, Zenith tells the Discord app running on this PC, over Discord's own local connection, how many Roblox clients it sees running, and Discord shows that in your status while Zenith runs; Zenith sends nothing over the internet for this. Discord shows a status only under an application: create one at discord.com/developers/applications, give it the name you want shown, and paste its Application ID below (a public ID, not a secret). Only a change is sent; when Discord is not running nothing is sent and Zenith checks again when the count changes or once a minute. The status is cleared when the dashboard is locked, by Panic and at exit, and shown again after Unlock or Resume Discord status. Save settings to apply.

data.name: Appearance_DiscordPresenceGame
data.value: Include the game in the Discord status

data.name: Appearance_DiscordPresenceGameDescription
data.value: Off by default. When on, the status also names the game the running clients are in, from what Zenith already knows (a favorite's name or a recently played name; otherwise the place ID), or says how many different games they are in. Nothing is looked up for it. Save settings to apply.

data.name: Appearance_DiscordApplicationIdTooltip
data.value: The 17 to 20 digit Application ID from the Discord Developer Portal; empty shows nothing

data.name: Appearance_ResumeDiscordPresenceTooltip
data.value: Show the status again after Panic or a refused application ID

data.name: Appearance_PanicShortcutDescription
data.value: F12 by default. Type an F-key (F1 to F24) on its own or with Ctrl, Alt or Shift, or Ctrl with a letter or digit, such as Ctrl+Alt+Shift+P. The shortcut takes its keys from every program, so combinations that type or edit there are not accepted: Ctrl+Alt with a letter or digit but without Shift (it is AltGr on many keyboards), Alt with a letter or digit but without Ctrl, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V and the other editing keys, F1 on its own, F10, Shift+F10, Alt+F4 and the Windows key. Save settings to register it for every program; if Windows refuses it, the shortcut that works stays registered. F12 keeps working while this window is focused, and the Panic button is always available.

data.name: Appearance_KeepAwakeDescription
data.value: Off by default. When on and saved, every chosen gap (5 to 19 minutes; Roblox disconnects a client after 20 idle minutes) Zenith brings each client forward, sends it one F13 press through its single input owner, and puts the window that was in front back. It waits while you have used the keyboard or mouse in the last 10 seconds. It is refused until the live input isolation trial marks background input Supported; until then this choice only shows why nothing runs. Panic and Lock stop it until you choose Resume keeping clients awake. Save settings to apply.
